content.text:
The new receipt email is now behind a feature flag, but the new email itself doesn't exist yet, so turning the flag on would break receipts until it's added.

**What changed:** in `services/notifier/notifier/email.py`, `send_receipt` uses a new `receipt_v2` template when the environment variable `NOTIFIER_FF_RECEIPT_V2` is `"1"`. Otherwise it keeps using the current `receipt` template. The notifier runs as its own service and can't read the main `flags.toml` or `flags.is_on()`, so it follows the notifier's own convention of `NOTIFIER_FF_<NAME>` environment variables.

**Tests:** the test in `tests/test_email.py` now checks three cases: flag unset, `"0"` and `"1"`. All 3 pass.

**Before you turn it on:**
1. **Add the new email.** There's no `receipt_v2` template in the repo, and no templates folder at all yet. Per the template convention, it needs `services/notifier/templates/receipt_v2.mjml` plus a plain-text twin, `receipt_v2.txt`, using the same variables (`invoice_id`, `total_minor`). If the new email already exists under another name or needs different data, tell me and I'll update the switch. Also, `render()` itself still raises `NotImplementedError`, so no email can be rendered yet, old or new.
2. **"Gradual" only works per deployment.** An environment-variable flag is on or off for a whole deployment of the notifier, so you can roll out by environment (staging first, then prod) but not by a percentage of customers. If you want a percentage rollout, I can add a bucket based on a hash of `invoice_id`, for example a `NOTIFIER_FF_RECEIPT_V2_PERCENT` setting.
